questions.question: If architecture barely matters compared to scale, why does the scaling hypothesis still require finding a 'scalable architecture' first?

passages.quote: a magnificently obsolete architecture from early 2018 (used mostly for software engineering convenience as the infrastructure has been debugged), which is small & shallow compared to what’s possible

questions.question: If GPT-3 is 'just' predicting text, how can that count as real understanding or intelligence?

passages.quote: It is ‘just’ a text prediction model, an idiot savant of text; but an idiot savant, we should remember, is only a genetic mutation or bit of brain damage away from a normal human.
if we ever succeed in AI, or in reductionism in general, it must be by reducing Y to ‘just X’.

questions.question: Isn't GPT-3 too costly to justify scaling up even further?

passages.quote: can ML afford to run projects which cost more than 0.1 milli-Manhattan-Projects⸮
Nonetheless, I think we can expect further scaling.

questions.question: Why would making a model bigger make it generalize better instead of just memorizing more of its training data?

passages.quote: Why do larger models not overfit (though they can) and generalize better than smaller models?
sub-models which memorize pieces of the data, or latch onto superficial features, learn quickest and are the easiest to represent internally.
it can’t possibly memorize all the instances of arithmetic (implicit or explicit) in GPT-3’s Internet-scale dataset.

questions.question: Since nobody can say what capabilities a further scaled-up model would gain, how confident can we be that scaling keeps working?

passages.quote: If GPT-3 gained so much meta-learning and world knowledge by dropping its absolute loss ~50% when starting from GPT-2’s level, what capabilities would another ~30% improvement over GPT-3 gain?
I don’t know.

questions.question: If major labs already have the hardware to match GPT-3, why hasn't an AI arms race already broken out?

passages.quote: The existence of the hardware overhang implies that the limiting factor here is less hardware than human: will any organization treat GPT-3 as a Sputnik moment and invest aggressively in scaling programs?
At least as of 2020-10-26, 152 days later, no model has come near GPT-3, and indeed, no model has even exceeded Turing-NLG’s 17b.

questions.question: If scale really is the secret to intelligence, why haven't well-funded rivals like DeepMind already built their own GPT-3-scale model?

passages.quote: they do not have any such thing, because Google Brain & DeepMind do not believe in the scaling hypothesis the way that Sutskever, Amodei and others at OA do.
they believe that AGI will require us to “find the right algorithms” effectively replicating a mammalian brain module by module

questions.question: Could we make a generative model safely non-agentic just by removing human-generated 'agentic' data from its training set?

passages.quote: would we then have a model which is now just a (relatively) safe ‘tool AI’, with no agency lurking?
agency is not a discrete thing, but a continuum, which is a convergent instrumental drive / emergent capability because it is useful even for understanding “non-agentic” things.
there cannot be any principled, hard-and-fast, necessary distinction between data which is ‘agentic’ and data which is merely ‘natural’.

questions.question: Does training on a single random computer program risk producing agent-like behavior the same way training on human text does?

passages.quote: There is nothing that random TM programs try to minimize or maximize; they simply run.
This provides our modularity, and a particular computation executed, and strong optimization pressure to rapidly ‘read’ the history and infer what the new rules must be.

questions.question: Doesn't saying almost any system can be read as agent-like prove too much, making the whole idea of 'agency' meaningless?

passages.quote: Agency may be like Turing-completeness: even in settings free of selection or optimization, it is a capability too useful and too convergent to guarantee its absence.
that there is no overt agency doesn’t mean it is not there.
